title: Broadcom Reports Earnings Today. At $2.25 Trillion, It Is the Biggest AI Chip Test of the Quarter.
excerpt: Wall Street expects $22.1 billion in revenue and $2.40 in adjusted EPS — both records — as the chipmaker's AI business doubles and oil prices push past $97 in the background.
body:
Broadcom reports its fiscal second-quarter earnings after market close on Wednesday, and the numbers Wall Street expects would have been unthinkable two years ago: $22.1 billion in revenue, up 47 per cent year over year, and adjusted earnings per share of $2.40, up 52 per cent from a year earlier. Both would be company records.

The report is the most consequential AI earnings event of the week, landing on a day when oil prices are threatening $98 a barrel, the OECD has warned that the Iran conflict could slow global growth to crisis-era levels, and the European Central Bank is widely expected to hike rates next week.

## The AI Revenue Machine

Broadcom's AI business has become the company's defining story. In the first quarter, AI semiconductor revenue hit $8.4 billion — up 106 per cent year over year. The company guided for $10.7 billion in the second quarter, a number that implies AI now accounts for nearly half of total revenue.

CEO Hock Tan has made a bold prediction: $100 billion in AI chip revenue by fiscal 2027. To get there, Broadcom is leaning on two pillars. The first is custom AI chips, known as application-specific integrated circuits, designed for six major customers including Alphabet and OpenAI. The Alphabet partnership alone spans a decade and eight generations of Google's Tensor Processing Unit chips.

The second pillar is AI networking — the switches and routers that connect thousands of chips inside hyperscale data centres. Broadcom expects networking to make up 40 per cent of AI revenue this quarter, the top end of its historical range. Its Tomahawk and Jericho product lines are the industry standard, though Nvidia's NVLink is a growing competitor.

On Monday, Alphabet announced an $80 billion equity raise to fund its AI spending, with $10 billion coming from Berkshire Hathaway. The company expects to spend up to $190 billion on capital expenditure this year. Broadcom is directly downstream of that spending, and its stock rose 4.7 per cent the following day.

## The Oil Shadow

Broadcom's earnings arrive against a backdrop that is becoming harder for markets to ignore. Brent crude climbed to $97.56 on Wednesday morning after Iranian missiles damaged Kuwait's airport and the US military struck sites near the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway remains effectively closed to non-Iranian shipping, choking off roughly a fifth of global oil and LNG flows.

The OECD warned on Wednesday that the conflict could slow global growth to rates rarely seen outside of major crises, while pushing inflation sharply higher. Markets have now priced in roughly 18 basis points of US rate increases this year — a stark reversal from the rate cuts expected just months ago.

For tech investors, the tension is between AI-driven earnings growth and a macroeconomic environment that is tightening fast. Broadcom's stock is up roughly 30 per cent year to date, more than double the S&P 500's gain, and options traders are pricing in a move of about 10.65 per cent in either direction after the report.

## What NRI Investors Should Watch

For Indian-origin investors holding US tech through brokerage accounts, 401(k) plans, or direct equity, Broadcom's report distils the two forces pulling at portfolios right now.

On one side: AI spending is accelerating. Alphabet's $80 billion raise, Meta naming Broadcom as its custom chip provider, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang calling Marvell Technology the next trillion-dollar company are all signs that the infrastructure buildout is not slowing down.

On the other: oil at $97 affects everything from grocery bills to remittance value. A weaker rupee — already under pressure from elevated crude imports — erodes the purchasing power of money sent home. If the Fed does hike rates, mortgage costs for NRI homebuyers in the US rise further, while Indian IT services companies face margin pressure from a stronger dollar.

Broadcom's guidance for the third quarter will matter more than the second-quarter beat. A raise would signal that AI demand is outrunning macro headwinds. A hold — or worse, a miss on networking — could trigger the kind of correction that options markets are bracing for.

The report drops after 4 PM Eastern. If you own tech in any form, it is worth watching.

**Sources**: Broadcom Investor Relations, Q1 FY2026 earnings; Reuters, "Oil extends gains as Middle East hostilities flare" (June 3, 2026); Barron's, "Broadcom Stock Faces Earnings Test" (June 3, 2026); Susquehanna analyst note (June 2, 2026).
